text:
oma_support: Flagging NeuroLabs billing question. Their May invoice shows 10 nodes reserved but an extra ~24 node-hours billed as burst across 05/14 during a regional failover. They say they didn't scale beyond their commit. Can ops/finance triage?

ryan_fin: Thanks. Drop invoice excerpt and reserved pool id so I can start the ticket.

oma_support: INV-2026-0514 in support case NL-9001. Reserved pool id: neuro-res-10. Billing snippet from system:
Invoice: INV-2026-0514
Period: 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-31
 - Reserved capacity (neuro-res-10): 10 nodes - $20,000
 - Burst usage (burst-unallocated): 24 node-hours - $360
Total: $20,360

billing-bot: Meter export attached for neuro-9001 (meter_export_2026_05_14.csv).

leo_ops: Quick look: there was a short cross-account pool_id collision during a failover window. A transient controller bug reused a recently deleted pool_id that belonged to a different org in us-east-2; our aggregator merged those rows into burst-unallocated when it couldn't reconcile the owner. So hours were not doubled, they were misattributed.

pete_engineering: Confirming. Controller patch (fixes pool id reuse) is ready; root cause was a race in pool cleanup + id namespace reuse. I can produce a CSV with node_id, ts, seen_pool_id, org_id to support re-association.

nina_sales: NeuroLabs is on an enterprise plan; relationship sensitive. Sales wants a clear timeline and a customer credit proposal. If we do a goodwill credit, keep wording precise (not an admission beyond meter error).

lina_revops: For audit we'll need the exported CSV and any backfill job ids attached to revops ticket. Also define internal reason codes for credits.

ryan_fin: Estimate delta once we get the CSV. Finance policy: manager approval up to $2,500; anything above needs VP approval. Prepare two numbers: invoice correction and optional SLA goodwill.

pete_engineering: CSV exported (neuro_pool_collision_05_14.csv). Summary: 24 node-hours misattributed -> invoice delta $360. All rows qualify for safe re-association. Backfill planned id bf-2026-621.

leo_ops: Backfill scheduled and limited to the 05/14 window. We'll re-tag rows to neuro-res-10 and update meter joins. Patch deployed to prevent pool_id reuse.

nina_sales: Sales proposes invoice adj $360 + goodwill SLA credit $1,500 = $1,860 total. That's within finance manager approval but we should consider adding a small service credit for impact to queuing delays during failover. Any engineering confirmation of degradation?

pete_engineering: We saw a brief p95 latency bump (~150ms) for 18 minutes during the failover window. Not service-wide but noticeable. Ops suggests $1,500 goodwill is reasonable.

ryan_fin: I can approve up to $2,500. So manager approves invoice correction $360 + service credit $1,500. I'll create credit memos: CM-2026-211 (INV adj $360) and CM-2026-212 (Service credit $1,500). Reason codes: POOL_ID_COLLISION & GOODWILL_SLA. Accounting: post to May ledger.

lina_revops: Revops ticket revops-856 created; attachments: neuro_pool_collision_05_14.csv, backfill bf-2026-621. Audit trail captured.

billing-bot: Created credit memos: CM-2026-211 (360), CM-2026-212 (1,500). Queued for AP posting.

oma_support: Draft customer message: "We identified a transient pool identifier collision during a regional failover that caused 24 node-hours to be misattributed. We've corrected the records and issued a $360 invoice adjustment and a $1,500 service credit. We've deployed a fix to prevent recurrence. Apologies for the disruption; credits will appear within 48h." Sending after AP posts.

vp_finance: Quick note: thanks for the check. No VP escalation needed here. Approve the memos for posting.

billing-bot: Credits posted to NeuroLabs account neuro-9001: CM-2026-211, CM-2026-212. Expected ledger posting date: 2026-05-16.

oma_support: Sent message to customer. Customer replied: "Thanks, appreciate the quick resolution." :white_check_mark:

ryan_fin: AP confirmed posting; closing ticket. Good cross-team response.
